fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 20 that a facility at the Moscow oil refinery was damaged after several drones reached the refinery premises during what Moscow authorities described as an unprecedented Ukrainian drone attack.

Reuters reported Russia said more than 1,600 drones had been downed since Saturday, including 450 headed for Moscow; the precise damage and resulting refinery operating-rate impact were not yet known.

Associated Press independently reported damage to the Moscow oil refinery during the large-scale attack and said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described critical oil and logistics targets as objectives of the strike.

Reuters noted that attacks on Russian refining capacity have already contributed to petroleum-product shortages, higher fuel prices and supply disruption in parts of Russia; the Moscow plant processed 11.6 million metric tons of crude in 2024, according to the latest data cited by Reuters.
semantic_interpretation: This is a material escalation in the Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure campaign because a major refinery serving the Russian capital was physically hit during the largest reported drone assault on Moscow. It increases refined-product and war-risk pressure and weakens confidence in the recently discussed energy-infrastructure restraint. The event is not treated as a quantified global oil-supply loss because the extent of damage, outage duration and current refinery throughput have not been independently established.
notes: Do not infer outage volume or duration until independently verified. Official numeric macro series remain authoritative.
